title: Will CoreWeave Stock Investors Get Swallowed by its Debt? | CRWV Stock
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc examines whether CoreWeave's debt load will swallow investors, concluding the risk-reward is attractive - but only for very high risk tolerance. The company held $6.5bn in cash at 30 September and expects ~$9bn of customer prepayments and deposits in the next three months, a new funding source as debt costs rise; prepayments make contracts less attractive to hyperscalers, who may build data centres themselves. Debt splits into asset-level secured debt (backed by customer contracts and infrastructure, still trading near par) and riskier unsecured parent-level debt. 2026 revenue guidance was raised to ~$13.15bn with adjusted operating income of $1.325bn, but capex is planned at ~$38bn - roughly 300% of revenue. Management expects adjusted net losses to shrink meaningfully in 2027 and turn to adjusted net income in 2028, with pricing rising to $20-25m per megawatt on long contracts. He reiterates his BUY (upgraded 14 October, restated earlier today at ~$50) with a $93 DCF fair value against a ~$61 price, noting demand still exceeds capacity and the company is largely sold out through 2027.
